questions.question: When you are riding in a vehicle's blind spot, what should you do?

options.text: Stay where you are so you don't surprise the driver.
Wave at the other driver to get their attention.
Slow down and move out of the blind spot.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and move out of the blind spot.
questions.explanation: If you are in a vehicle's blind spot, you should speed up quickly or slow down to leave the spot.

questions.question: How should a group of riders pass another vehicle?
questions.correctAnswerText: One at a time.
questions.explanation: On a two-lane highway, riders should pass one at a time. The next rider should wait until the first rider is safely back in the original lane before passing.

questions.question: When carrying a heavy load, what should you adjust?
questions.correctAnswerText: Suspension.
questions.explanation: Before carrying a heavy load, adjust your tire pressure, spring pre-load, air shocks, and dampers to the settings recommended for that weight.

questions.question: What type of sign is rectangular?
questions.correctAnswerText: Speed limit sign.
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs like speed limits are rectangular and white with black letters or symbols. You must follow the rules on these signs.

questions.question: What is a danger of riding directly alongside another vehicle?

options.text: You may be in the driver's blind spot.
It is safer than riding behind the other vehicle.
It is safe because it limits your escape routes.
It should only be done during the day.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may be in the driver's blind spot.
questions.explanation: Avoid riding directly alongside another vehicle because the driver may not see you. The vehicle also blocks your escape route if a hazard appears.

questions.question: Where should you place a load on a motorcycle?

options.text: On one side of the motorcycle

questions.correctAnswerText: As low as possible
questions.explanation: Keep loads low and secure them in saddlebags. High loads raise the motorcycle's center of gravity and affect balance. Distribute loads equally on both sides.

questions.question: Why should a load be placed low on a motorcycle?

options.text: A high load raises the center of gravity.
A high load may block the turn signals.
You may not be able to see over a high load.
Others can't see your load if it is low.

questions.correctAnswerText: A high load raises the center of gravity.
questions.explanation: A high load raises the motorcycle's center of gravity and can upset its balance.

questions.question: Which of the following does NOT reduce your chances of an accident?

options.text: Identifying hazards and deciding what to address first.

questions.correctAnswerText: Riding without a headlight.
questions.explanation: To avoid crashes, stay alert, identify hazards, use your headlight to be visible, and maintain space around your motorcycle.

questions.question: What should you do when riding on a slippery surface?

options.text: Move to the edge of the road.
Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.
questions.explanation: On slippery surfaces, slow down, avoid sudden moves, stay away from the road edge, and ride in tire tracks left by other cars.

questions.question: If a tire goes flat while riding, what should you do?

options.text: Relax your grip on the handle grips.
Shift your weight toward the good tire.
Brake on the good tire and steer to the side of the road.
Use both brakes and stop quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake on the good tire and steer to the side of the road.
questions.explanation: Hold the handle grips firmly, ease off the throttle, and go straight. Gradually brake on the good tire. Edge to the side of the road, pull in the clutch, and stop.

questions.question: When riding in a group, what is the best way to stay close while keeping safe distance between riders?
questions.correctAnswerText: In a staggered formation.
questions.explanation: A staggered formation lets riders stay close while keeping safe distance between them. Use a single-file line when riding on curves, turning, or entering or leaving a highway. Never ride side-by-side with another rider.

questions.question: Where should inexperienced riders position themselves in a group?

options.text: At the rear of the group.

questions.correctAnswerText: Just behind the leader.
questions.explanation: Inexperienced riders should position themselves just behind the leader. This allows more experienced riders behind them to watch and help if needed.

questions.question: What color vest or jacket helps other drivers see you best?
questions.correctAnswerText: Red
questions.explanation: Bright colors help other drivers see you. Bright red, orange, yellow, or green are best. Dark or dull colors are harder for other drivers to see.

questions.question: What should you focus on when adjusting your mirrors?

options.text: The road behind and to the side of your motorcycle.
The road in front of your motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road behind and to the side of your motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Adjust your mirrors to see the lane behind you and as much as possible of the lane next to you. You may see part of your arm or shoulder, but the road behind and beside you is most important.

questions.question: What happens when your rear tire skids?

options.text: You lose the ability to change direction.
It is only a problem if the front tire also skids.

questions.correctAnswerText: You lose the ability to change direction.
questions.explanation: A skidding rear tire is dangerous and can cause a serious crash. Too much rear brake pressure can lock the rear wheel. When the rear wheel locks, you cannot change direction. Release the brake to regain control.

questions.question: What happens if you shift to a lower gear while going too fast?

options.text: Your motorcycle may lurch and the rear tire may skid.
Your motorcycle may lurch and the front tire may skid.
Your motorcycle may lurch and a warning light will go on.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your motorcycle may lurch and the rear tire may skid.
questions.explanation: Shifting to a lower gear while going too fast can cause your motorcycle to lurch and the rear tire to skid, causing you to lose control. Slow down enough before shifting to a lower gear.

questions.question: If you must ride over an obstacle, what should you do?

options.text: Decrease your speed as much as possible.
Lean the motorcycle to one side.
Stay on your seat and remove your feet from the footrests.

questions.correctAnswerText: Decrease your speed as much as possible.
questions.explanation: If you cannot avoid an obstacle, slow down and approach it straight on if possible. Keep your motorcycle upright. Just before hitting it, ease off the throttle to lighten the front end.

questions.question: What is true about approved helmets?

options.text: They let the rider see far enough to the sides for safe riding.
You do not have to wear one if you think it limits your view.

questions.correctAnswerText: They let the rider see far enough to the sides for safe riding.
questions.explanation: Some people worry that helmets limit their view, but this is not true. Approved helmets let riders see far enough to the sides for safe riding.

questions.question: A person drinks 7 drinks in 3 hours. The body removes about 1 drink per hour. How many drinks are likely still in their system 3 hours after their last drink?
questions.correctAnswerText: Four
questions.explanation: Subtract the hours passed since the last drink from the total drinks consumed. In this case: 7 drinks minus 3 hours equals 4 drinks remaining in the system.

questions.question: Why should you avoid riding alongside another rider?

options.text: It allows you to maximize the surface of the road.
It limits your escape routes if there is a hazard.
It allows you to communicate with one another.
It makes it easier for other motorists to pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: It limits your escape routes if there is a hazard.
questions.explanation: Do not ride alongside another rider because it limits both riders' escape routes if a hazard appears.

questions.question: How much of a motorcycle's total braking power comes from the front brake?
questions.correctAnswerText: About 70 percent
questions.explanation: The front brake is more powerful than the rear brake. It provides at least three-quarters of the motorcycle's total stopping power.

questions.question: When stopping, what should you do?

options.text: Apply both brakes at the same time.
Use only one brake, front or rear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Apply both brakes at the same time.
questions.explanation: Use both brakes every time you slow down or stop. Always apply the brakes together at the same time.

questions.question: What type of clothing material offers the best protection for motorcyclists?
questions.correctAnswerText: Leather
questions.explanation: Leather clothing provides the best protection for motorcyclists. Always wear clothing that covers your legs and arms completely when riding.

questions.question: If you need to stop quickly while turning, what should you do?

options.text: Straighten the handlebars and then stop.
Apply both brakes hard while leaning.

questions.correctAnswerText: Straighten the handlebars and then stop.
questions.explanation: If you must stop quickly while turning, first straighten the handlebars, then stop. If you cannot straighten your motorcycle, apply the brakes smoothly and gradually. Reduce your lean angle and increase brake pressure as you slow down.

questions.question: When riding downhill or shifting into first gear, what may you need to do?

options.text: Use your brakes to slow down before shifting to a lower gear.
Speed up before shifting to a lower gear.
Flash your brakes to warn drivers behind you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your brakes to slow down before shifting to a lower gear.
questions.explanation: Slow down to a safe speed before shifting into a lower gear. Downshifting while going too fast can cause the motorcycle to jerk and the rear wheel to skid. Use your brakes to reach a safe speed before downshifting.

questions.question: What does making eye contact with another driver mean?

options.text: The other driver will definitely yield to you.
It is not worth the effort.
The other driver may not yield to you.
The other driver knows you are there.

questions.correctAnswerText: The other driver may not yield to you.
questions.explanation: Do not assume that eye contact means another driver will yield the right-of-way to you. Never count on it.

questions.question: If your motorcycle starts to wobble, what should you do?

options.text: Hold the handlebars firmly and slowly close the throttle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold the handlebars firmly and slowly close the throttle.
questions.explanation: Do not speed up, as this will make the wobble worse. Instead, grip the handlebars firmly and slowly close the throttle to slow down. Lean forward and downward, and pull off the road as soon as possible. Avoid braking, as it may make the wobble worse.

questions.question: When riding with a passenger, what should you do?

options.text: Try to squeeze into smaller gaps in traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride more slowly than usual.
questions.explanation: A passenger adds weight and changes how your motorcycle handles. Your motorcycle will accelerate slower, turn slower, and need more distance to stop. Ride more slowly, start slowing sooner when approaching stops, keep a larger space cushion, and wait for larger gaps in traffic.

questions.question: What formation helps keep group riders closest together?
questions.correctAnswerText: Staggered
questions.explanation: A staggered formation helps a group stay close while allowing each rider to maintain safe distance. Use single-file formation when taking curves, turning, or entering or exiting a highway.

questions.question: If your front tire goes flat while riding, what will happen to the steering?

options.text: There will be no change in the steering.
The ride will feel too smooth.

questions.correctAnswerText: The steering will feel heavy.
questions.explanation: A flat front tire will make the steering feel heavy. If your steering feels heavy, exit the road right away and check your tires.
